messages:
leigh: Quick heads-up — our 30d forecast shows a ~17% delta between hosted API GPU demand and our reserved commitments in eu-west. Putting a link to the model + chart: https://redwood.share/forecast-1749998888 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

dan: can you paste the topline numbers here? /cc finance-ops

leigh: sure — top-line snapshot: ```reserved: 1,200 GPU-hrs/day
forecasted hosted demand: 1,400 GPU-hrs/day
peak day demand: 2,100 GPU-hrs
avg shortfall: 200 GPU-hrs/day
95pct shortfall: 900 GPU-hrs```

finance-ops: :eyes: Oof. When does this start to hit?

leigh: shortfalls begin in ~12 days, ramping over ~3 weeks if current growth continues (chat + embeddings growth). This already includes current cache savings (~13% token reduction).

dan: is the forecast adjusted for upcoming batching and the autoscaler headroom? we shouldn't double-count improvements.

leigh: baseline includes current caching. it does NOT include the batching patch we have queued — batching expected next week.

priya: estimated impact of batching patch?

leigh: conservative estimate: 8–12% reduction in effective GPU-hrs for gen traffic. That would close ~60% of the avg shortfall but won't eliminate 95th pct peaks.

finance-ops: what's the incremental cost if we handle the delta with on-demand for 30d? rough calc?

dan: quick calc (ballpark): sustained avg shortfall = 200 GPU-hrs/day -> 6,000 GPU-hrs/mo. on-demand ~ $2.4/hr -> ~$14.4k/month. peak events (900 GPU-hrs) are smaller in frequency but add spikes. reserved commit addition would be capitalized differently.

priya: mitigation options I propose: 1) push batching rollout (low risk) 2) shift a few nodes from non-prod pools 3) temporarily throttle non-critical embedding routes during peaks 4) finance to model short-term top-up commit vs on-demand

leigh: also consider quick quantization for embedder-v2 (we saw ~15% throughput improvement in bench) — needs ML QA but could be a mid-term delta closer.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance in eu-west at 1749999900 has been cancelled due to elevated capacity pressure.

dan: operational timeline: we can release batching tomorrow AM, reassign 3 reserved nodes from staging by EOD, and flip the throttle flag on non-critical routes when shortfall > 300 for >1h.

finance-ops: I'll run a breakeven calc for buying +10% reserved capacity vs on-demand for next 3 months and post numbers in ~2h.

priya: legal/ops: can we repurpose Dedicated customer pools temporarily if they're idle? That needs legal review and customer opt-in, but worth checking.

leigh: do NOT touch Dedicated customers without explicit approval. We should exhaust infra+non-prod and throttles first.

dan: TL;DR action items: leigh -> push batching PR and monitor; priya -> prepare throttle config + runbook; finance-ops -> cost comparison; dan -> reassign staging nodes and set shortfall alert. I'll spin up a short-lived channel for real-time triage.

priya: ack. creating calendar block "capacity-triage" 17:00 UTC today.

finance-ops: posted breakeven: add 10% commit (est) = $52k/mo vs expected incremental on-demand = $68k/mo -> if growth sustains beyond ~6 weeks, commit is cheaper.

leigh: good data. let's wait one week after batching to see trend before locking commit.

dan: i'm setting an alert: shortfall_monitor -> fire when shortfall > 500 GPU-hrs for 3 consecutive hours.

infra-bot: Alert created: shortfall_monitor (threshold 500) -> PagerDuty oncall "infra-capacity".
